title: More And More Games Are Asking A Question Even Philosophers Haven't Been Able To Answer
description: Sunset Visitor's upcoming game Prove You're Human bears an ominous title. Its debut trailer is just as provocative as its name lets on, and introduces us to Mesa, a seemingly rogue AI who has dreamt of her body and needs irrefutable proof that she is not human. The upcoming title from the developer behind 2024's critically acclaimed sci-fi narrative 1000xResist purports to address a growing anxiety around the notion of human performance and things that try to pass for us. Elsewhere, a late-night worker at a gas station must check IDs and reference a database filled with the specific characteristics that make each customer who walks through its doors an individual. A person. As the only clerk on the midnight shift, they are tasked with distinguishing friend from foe, person from nonperson. And when the time comes to defend themself, they are encouraged to blast anything that would harm them or impersonate any real human. At least, that's the way of the world in the upcoming game Shift at Midnight, which has become a viral hit before it's even released thanks to a spate of demos and glowing coverage from popular gaming personalities, like Iron Lung director Mark "Markiplier" Fishbach. Shift at Midnight features creepy skinwalkers that stalk the gas station.I don't think Prove You're Human will suddenly become a guns-blazing first-person shooter, nor will Shift at Midnight begin waxing philosophically. Yet despite taking different tacts and centering distinct forms of mimicry, these titles are in conversation and represent the future, both near and far, of a trend I've noticed: the sounding of an alarm. title: Ambitious Hades 2 Mod Combines It With Everything From The First Game
description: Hades II is already a much bigger game that Supergiant's first entry in the series, but thanks to a new mod, it's set to grow substantially larger. Modder NikkelM has managed to cram the whole of Hades into its sequel in a far more elegant way than you would expect from a free, solo effort. The project, dubbed simply Zagreus Journey, lets you play through all of the content from Hades as its sequel's protagonist, Melinoe. This means revisiting areas such as Styx, Tartarus, Elysium, and more and go toe-to-toe with all the foes that likely caused hundreds of deaths the last time you stood against this. However, this time you're confronting them with an entirely new set of skills and weapons, with some new boons and abilities available from returning characters to help balance each encounter to suit its new heroine slightly. Letting you explore these areas again would be one thing, but the mod also elegantly weaves Melinoe into the story. Although characters still talk to Zagreus, the conceit here is that he's simply along for the ride, with Melinoe the one getting her hands dirty in-between. Seeing her present during conversations certainly helps ground her in a story that was previously written without her in mind, which is a nice touch. Continue Reading at GameSpot

As is usually the case, the key to these secret quests is always in the flavor text, and the flavor text for both of these items are leading players to believe Diablo 4's cow-themed shenanigans are just heating up. title: How Reality Fracture Will Push The Boundaries Of Magic The Gathering (And Its Printers)
description: One of Magic the Gathering's biggest releases of 2026, Reality Fracture, will see the franchise's iconic Planeswalker Jace create the Echoverse, a mirrored version of the current MTG universe in which world-defining events have been rewritten. In a press Q&A at this year's MagicCon Vegas, Magic head designer Mark Rosewater said that a "What If" set has been one of the most requested by fans in the franchise's history, and Reality Fracture satisfies that need. However, while the Echoverse creates a ton of possibilities, this release will intentionally be very focused. "Very early on, we were talking about maybe going broader," Rosewater said. "But we decided that one of the lessons from March of the Machines was we went a little bit too broad, and we decided we wanted to focus a little bit more. So, we'll see nods about [other] places, but really, the story is on Hexhaven." Hexhaven is Reality Fracture's version of Strixhaven, which was the focus of the latest Magic release Secrets of Strixhaven. Typically, when one corner of the MTG multiverse is explored in a set, the subsequent releases will revolve around a completely different part of the lore, making Wizard of the Coast's choice to return to the college an unusual one for the game; this decision could easily risk inundating players with too much scholarly content. However, Rosewater reassured me that while Hexhaven is central to Reality Fracture, this set will be different from them doing a Hexhaven-focused set. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Mortal Kombat 2 Reviews Are Split Down The Middle, And For Once That's Literal
description: After a lengthy wait and a last-minute delay, Mortal Kombat 2 is finally bicycle-kicking its way into theaters this week. The sequel to 2021's Mortal Kombat has been promising bigger fights, deeper lore dives, and Karl Urban hamming it up as fan-favorite character Johnny Cage, but what do the early reviews say? Currently, they're more divided than one of Kung Lao's opponents after they've been subjected to his fatality. GameSpot's sister site Metacritic has begun gathering up reviews, and so far, the metascore aggregate is sitting on a dead-average 50 from 21 sites at the time of writing. This number will change as more reviews go live over the next few weeks, but it looks like opinions are all over the place when it comes to Mortal Kombat 2. When it comes to positive reviews, IGN called Mortal Kombat 2 a showcase of "big and loud" action, while SlashFilm described the sequel as one of the biggest surprises of the year. On the opposite end of the review spectrum, outlets like The AV Club described it as a campy mess without any heart, Radio Times labeled Mortal Kombat 2 as a serviceable follow-up at best, and Variety says the movie is all style without any real substance. The lack of a cohesive story appears to be one of the major complaints from reviewers, but Urban's portrayal as a washed-up martial arts movie star drafted into protecting the realms has been generally well-received. title: Mina The Hollower Finally Has A Release Date, At Long Last
description: Four years ago, Yacht Club Games announced Mina The Hollower, a retro pixel-art adventure game starring a cute little mouse in a hellish world of monsters. Evoking the style of old Game Boy Legend of Zelda games, Mina quickly grew to become one of the most highly anticipated indie titles in gaming. Today, Yacht Club Games finally confirmed what those fans have longed to hear: After multiple delays, Mina The Hollower has a release date of May 29--a mere 23 days away--and a price tag of $20. Yacht Club made the announcement on social media, delivering both the release date and price via a post and a small teaser video. title: Diablo In Diablo 4? It Could Still Be A While (Or Possibly Never)
description: Diablo 4's Lord of Hatred expansion brings a conclusive end to the storyline started in the base game of Blizzard's live-service ARPG, but already players are wondering what comes next. According to those following Diablo 4's lore, it might not be Diablo himself. Spoilers for Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred below. Mephisto's defeat in the expansion brings an end to the Age of Hatred, wrapping up the storyline that started in 2023 with Diablo 4's release. Lilith is gone for the time being, having been defeated in the base game, and her connection to the player-character severed in Lord of Hatred. Mephisto is sent into the Void, from which he can't reform in hell. That leaves a bit of a power vacuum in Sanctuary, and while many fans would likely love to see the franchise's namesake appear as the next big bad of Diablo 4, the more likely candidate is Baal, the Lord of Destruction.
